newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police start rfresh hunt for dead children.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police start rfresh hunt for dead children.

text.p: Belgian police, acting on fresh information, started a new hunt on Friday in the southern town of Charleroi for the bodies of children who have gone missing in the past seven years, possible victims of a paedophile ring.

"Based on information from some of the arrested people, and certain enquiries we have been able to make, we are convinced that here at (the suburb of) Jumet...not far from the tunnel we searched in (October), there is another underground place where we may find traces of children or somewhere they were held," Gendarmerie Major Marcel Guissard told RTBF television.

Commander Johan Dewinne, who heads the body identification team of the gendarmerie, told BRTN radio police were looking for several bodies. He said he was more hopeful of finding victims than during the previous search in the area.
VTM television later said guns had been found.
A police spokesman told Reuters the searches were stopped at the end of the afternoon as darkness set in, but would be resumed at daybreak on Saturday. The area searched was sealed off by police.
Police searched a scrap metal yard, towing away several car wrecks, but focused attention on four houses whose basements might be linked to another mine shaft.
The hunt in October, based on information from chief suspect, convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux, found nothing.
VTM said that Dutroux and his second wife Michelle Martin had once lived in one of the houses.
Belgium has been in shock since mid-August when Dutroux and several alleged accomplices were arrested.
Police rescued two young girls from a secret dungeon in the basement of a house owned by Dutroux in the Marcinelle suburb of Charleroi. Both had been sexually abused.

Just two days later Dutroux led police to the bodies of two eight-year-old girls -- Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo -- buried alongside that of a former Dutroux accomplice Bernard Weinstein in the garden of another of six Dutroux homes in and around the town.
The girls, missing for 14 months, had starved to death.

Less than three weeks later Dutroux led investigators to Weinstein's former house in Jumet where extensive digging unearthed the bodies of An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks who had been missing for a year.
Dutroux, Martin, Michel Nihoul, Michel Lelievre and Mikael Diakostavrianos remain in prison while investigations continue.

Police, who are searching for at least another seven missing children, on Tuesday charged another man, Jacques Genevoix, in connection with the abduction in 1992 of a nine-year-old Moroccan girl, Loubna Benaissa.
BRTN television said that the parents of all missing children had been informed of the new search action.
